findings.title: Inside the Qubole Supply Chain Attack: How Sentra Found It
findings.summary_md: Sentra says it uncovered a broad supply chain attack in which an attacker used credentials belonging to Qubole to reach dozens of Qubole customers through IAM roles those customers still trusted. The company detected the activity across several customer environments, traced stolen files to Qubole roles that had been dormant since the spring, and reported it to Wiz, which investigated with Sentra and Mandiant. Sentra counts more than a dozen organizations hacked in a single attack and about 100 passwords and keys read in seven minutes, with zero write actions.

findings.title: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
findings.summary_md: Wiz CIRT reports that between October 14 and October 26, 2026, a threat actor used IAM credentials from AWS account 805246085872, associated with Qubole, to assume customer integration roles that still trusted the vendor account. The actor enumerated resources, harvested secrets from Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store, validated credentials with TruffleHog, and exfiltrated S3 data, sometimes downloading entire buckets in one session. Wiz states a source IP condition in the role trust policy would have blocked every role assumption it observed.

findings.title: Attackers backdoor trusted AWS integrations to steal secrets
findings.summary_md: The Register reports that attackers used compromised IAM credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments and steal secrets and data between October 14 and October 26, 2026. It notes Qubole integrations rely on cross-account IAM roles that customers configure to trust the vendor's account, and that Wiz observed a separate October 8-11 campaign using customer-owned AWS access keys. Qubole is described as a cloud data processing platform owned by Idera.
